evidence.finding: Mean adherence fell from 92.2% before the incident to 62.0% at/after onset, beginning at 09:15.
Mean productive staffing fell 32.8%, from 45.2 to 30.4 agents, while scheduled and logged-in staffing remained fixed at 49.
Mean service level declined from 88.0% before onset to 51.4% at/after onset.
Mean ASA rose from 28.7 to 79.2 seconds as productive capacity declined.
Post-onset volume averaged only 4.2% above forecast, making demand a contributor rather than the primary cause.
All four queues experienced service-level and ASA deterioration, indicating a center-wide capacity issue rather than an isolated queue problem.

primary_root_cause_detail: Adherence collapsed at incident onset, reducing mean productive staffing from 45.2 to 30.4 agents despite all 49 scheduled agents remaining logged in. This capacity loss explains the simultaneous center-wide increase in ASA and decline in service level.
recommended_actions: Identify and correct the agent-state or schedule-adherence behavior that began at 09:15.
Restore productive staffing to required levels through real-time adherence intervention, reserve activation, or intraday schedule changes.
Alert workforce management when productive staffing diverges materially from logged-in headcount.
Temporarily rebalance capacity toward Billing while its elevated volume persists.
Review adherence recovery and service-level normalization at 15-minute intervals.

rejected_hypotheses.reason: Volume averaged only 4.2% above forecast after onset, materially below the 32.8% productive-staffing reduction.
Mean AHT decreased after onset and averaged 0.7% below forecast.
Every queue degraded while queue staffing counts remained unchanged; the effect was not isolated to one queue.
Logged-in headcount and transfer rates remained stable, with no corroborating platform event.
The service-level decline was corroborated by higher ASA and abandonment, lower answered volume, and queue-level degradation.

stakeholder_summary: The service-level incident was most likely caused by a sharp adherence decline that removed roughly one-third of productive capacity while logged-in headcount stayed constant. A moderate volume increase added pressure, but demand, AHT, platform, and queue-specific explanations do not account for the center-wide sustained impact.
